# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

## Overview

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Feature Name**: String Slugification Utility
**Priority**: Must Have
**Target Users**: Developers using the utility module

### Summary

Add a pure utility function that converts arbitrary text strings into URL-safe slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.

### Business Context

URL-safe slugs are essential for creating readable, consistent identifiers in URLs, filenames, database keys, and routing systems. This utility will provide a standardized transformation that developers can rely on across the codebase.

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must convert all uppercase letters to lowercase.

**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase for consistency and to avoid case-sensitivity issues across different systems and browsers.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input "Hello World" produces output starting with "hello world" (before other transformations)
- Input "ABC123" produces output starting with "abc123"
- Mixed case input "FooBar" produces output starting with "foobar"

---

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens.

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, improving readability while maintaining URL safety. Both spaces (from natural text) and underscores (from identifiers) should be normalized to the same separator.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Single space " " is replaced with single hyphen "-"
- Multiple consecutive spaces "  " are replaced with single hyphen "-"
- Underscores "_" are replaced with hyphens "-"
- Double underscores "__" are replaced with single hyphen "-"
- Mixed whitespace and underscores are normalized to single hyphens

---

### REQ-003: Special Character Removal
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen.

**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause issues in URLs, filesystems, and databases. Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Exclamation marks "!" are removed from output
- Commas "," are removed from output
- Periods "." are removed from output
- Apostrophes "'" are removed from output
- Any punctuation or special characters not in [a-z0-9-] are removed
- Unicode/accented characters are removed (not transliterated)

---

### REQ-004: Hyphen Deduplication
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.

**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens can result from removing special characters between words or from consecutive whitespace. Collapsing them improves readability and consistency.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input "a---b" produces output "a-b"
- Input "a--b" produces output "a-b"
- Any sequence of two or more hyphens is replaced with exactly one hyphen
- This deduplication applies after all other character transformations

---

### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the final output.

**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at string boundaries. They serve no semantic purpose and should be removed for cleaner output.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input "-hello" produces output "hello"
- Input "hello-" produces output "hello"
- Input "-hello-" produces output "hello"
- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
- Interior hyphens are preserved

---

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Convert User Input to URL Slug
**As a** web application developer
**I want** to convert user-provided titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN a blog post title "Hello, World!"
- WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
- THEN I receive "hello-world"

---

### STORY-002: Normalize Identifier Strings
**As a** system integrator
**I want** to normalize mixed-format identifiers
**So that** I have consistent keys for database records or file names

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN an identifier "Foo__Bar  "
- WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar  ")
- THEN I receive "foo-bar"

---

### STORY-003: Clean Complex Input
**As a** data processing developer
**I want** to handle messy input with repeated delimiters
**So that** the output is always clean and predictable

**Acceptance Criteria**:

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-27

## Summary

Implement a pure `slugify` function in the existing utils module that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs through a sequential chain of string transformations: lowercase conversion, whitespace/underscore normalization to hyphens, special character removal, hyphen deduplication, and boundary trimming. The approach uses native JavaScript string methods and regex patterns with no external dependencies, maintaining consistency with the existing codebase patterns.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input String"] --> LC["toLowerCase()"]
    LC --> WS["Replace spaces/underscores"]
    WS --> SC["Remove special chars"]
    SC --> DD["Deduplicate hyphens"]
    DD --> TR["Trim boundary hyphens"]
    TR --> Output["Output Slug"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | utils.ts | Any module | `slugify(text: string): string` - returns URL-safe slug |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure string transformation function implementing all 5 requirements | `src/utils.ts` |
| T2 | slugify tests | Comprehensive unit tests covering all transformation rules and edge cases | `src/utils.test.ts` |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Function implementation has no dependencies

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (interface dependency: tests must import the slugify function)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Lowercase conversion | Uppercase chars remain | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello" -> "hello" |
| Space replacement | Spaces not converted | unit | `bun test` - verify "a b" -> "a-b" |
| Underscore replacement | Underscores not converted | unit | `bun test` - verify "a_b" -> "a-b" |
| Multiple whitespace collapse | Multiple hyphens from spaces | unit | `bun test` - verify "a  b" -> "a-b" |
| Special char removal | Invalid URL chars remain | unit | `bun test` - verify "a!b" -> "ab" |
| Hyphen deduplication | Multiple hyphens in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "a--b" -> "a-b" |
| Leading hyphen trim | Output starts with hyphen | unit | `bun test` - verify "-a" -> "a" |
| Trailing hyphen trim | Output ends with hyphen | unit | `bun test` - verify "a-" -> "a" |
| Empty string handling | Runtime error on empty | unit | `bun test` - verify "" -> "" |
| All special chars | Unexpected output | unit | `bun test` - verify "---" -> "" |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | modules.md | Utils section | modules.md:utils | Add slugify to documented utility functions |

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regex edge cases with unusual input | LOW | Comprehensive test coverage from requirements examples |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-27

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Transformation order | lowercase -> replace whitespace/underscores -> remove special chars -> dedupe hyphens -> trim | This order ensures each step processes the output of the previous step correctly. Lowercasing first simplifies the special char regex. Deduplication must happen after all replacements that could create hyphens. Trimming must be last. | Different orderings tested; this order minimizes redundant operations |
| D2 | Regex vs iterative | Single-pass regex replacements | Native regex in JavaScript is optimized and concise. Chain of replace() calls is idiomatic and readable. | Character-by-character iteration would be verbose and slower |
| D3 | Whitespace pattern | `/[\s_]+/g` | Matches all whitespace characters (space, tab, newline) plus underscores in one pattern. The `+` quantifier handles multiple consecutive occurrences. | Separate patterns for space and underscore would require two replace calls |
| D4 | Special char pattern | `/[^a-z0-9-]/g` | Negated character class removes everything except lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Applied after lowercase conversion so no need for A-Z. | Allowlist approach would be more verbose |
| D5 | Hyphen deduplication | `/-+/g` replaced with `-` | Matches one or more hyphens and replaces with single hyphen. Handles both deduplication and edge cases from special char removal. | Lookahead assertions would be more complex |
| D6 | Boundary trim approach | `replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')` | Single regex handles both leading and trailing hyphens. More concise than separate replace calls or trim-like functions. | Two separate replace calls; substring manipulation |

---

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |

| Implementation location | src/utils.ts | KB modules.md | KB specifies utils.ts as the designated location for pure reusable functions |

| TypeScript strictness | strict mode | KB patterns.md | Project enforces TypeScript strict mode |
| Dependencies | None (built-in string methods only) | Requirements constraint | Requirements explicitly prohibit external dependencies |

    11→## Overview

    13→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    14→**Feature Name**: String Slugification Utility
    15→**Priority**: Must Have
    16→**Target Users**: Developers using the utility module
    17→
    18→### Summary
    19→
    20→Add a pure utility function that converts arbitrary text strings into URL-safe slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    21→
    22→### Business Context
    23→
    24→URL-safe slugs are essential for creating readable, consistent identifiers in URLs, filenames, database keys, and routing systems. This utility will provide a standardized transformation that developers can rely on across the codebase.
    25→
    26→## Requirements
    27→
    28→### REQ-001: Text Normalization
    29→**Priority**: Must Have
    30→**User Type**: Developer
    31→**Description**: The slugify function must convert all uppercase letters to lowercase.
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase for consistency and to avoid case-sensitivity issues across different systems and browsers.
    34→
    35→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    36→- Input "Hello World" produces output starting with "hello world" (before other transformations)
    37→- Input "ABC123" produces output starting with "abc123"
    38→- Mixed case input "FooBar" produces output starting with "foobar"
    39→
    40→---
    41→
    42→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    43→**Priority**: Must Have
    44→**User Type**: Developer
    45→**Description**: The slugify function must replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    46→
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, improving readability while maintaining URL safety. Both spaces (from natural text) and underscores (from identifiers) should be normalized to the same separator.
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- Single space " " is replaced with single hyphen "-"
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces "  " are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    52→- Underscores "_" are replaced with hyphens "-"
    53→- Double underscores "__" are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    54→- Mixed whitespace and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    55→
    56→---
    57→
    58→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal
    59→**Priority**: Must Have
    60→**User Type**: Developer
    61→**Description**: The slugify function must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen.
    62→
    63→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause issues in URLs, filesystems, and databases. Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility.
    64→
    65→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    66→- Exclamation marks "!" are removed from output
    67→- Commas "," are removed from output
    68→- Periods "." are removed from output
    69→- Apostrophes "'" are removed from output
    70→- Any punctuation or special characters not in [a-z0-9-] are removed
    71→- Unicode/accented characters are removed (not transliterated)
    72→
    73→---
    74→
    75→### REQ-004: Hyphen Deduplication
    76→**Priority**: Must Have
    77→**User Type**: Developer
    78→**Description**: The slugify function must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    79→
    80→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens can result from removing special characters between words or from consecutive whitespace. Collapsing them improves readability and consistency.
    81→
    82→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    83→- Input "a---b" produces output "a-b"
    84→- Input "a--b" produces output "a-b"
    85→- Any sequence of two or more hyphens is replaced with exactly one hyphen
    86→- This deduplication applies after all other character transformations
    87→
    88→---
    89→
    90→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
    91→**Priority**: Must Have
    92→**User Type**: Developer
    93→**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the final output.
    94→
    95→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at string boundaries. They serve no semantic purpose and should be removed for cleaner output.
    96→
    97→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    98→- Input "-hello" produces output "hello"
    99→- Input "hello-" produces output "hello"
   100→- Input "-hello-" produces output "hello"
   101→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
   102→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   103→
   104→---

   106→## User Stories

   108→### STORY-001: Convert User Input to URL Slug
   109→**As a** web application developer

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Convert a string to a URL-safe slug.
 *
 * Transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs by:
 * - Converting to lowercase
 * - Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * - Removing non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
 * - Collapsing consecutive hyphens
 * - Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The input string to slugify
 * @returns A URL-safe slug string
 *
 * @example
 * slugify("Hello, World!") // returns "hello-world"
 * slugify("Foo__Bar  ") // returns "foo-bar"
 * slugify("a---b") // returns "a-b"
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, "")
    .replace(/-+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
}

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    14→**Feature Name**: String Slugification Utility
    15→**Priority**: Must Have
    16→**Target Users**: Developers using the utility module
    17→
    18→### Summary
    19→
    20→Add a pure utility function that converts arbitrary text strings into URL-safe slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    21→
    22→### Business Context
    23→
    24→URL-safe slugs are essential for creating readable, consistent identifiers in URLs, filenames, database keys, and routing systems. This utility will provide a standardized transformation that developers can rely on across the codebase.
    25→
    26→## Requirements
    27→
    28→### REQ-001: Text Normalization
    29→**Priority**: Must Have
    30→**User Type**: Developer
    31→**Description**: The slugify function must convert all uppercase letters to lowercase.
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase for consistency and to avoid case-sensitivity issues across different systems and browsers.
    34→
    35→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    36→- Input "Hello World" produces output starting with "hello world" (before other transformations)
    37→- Input "ABC123" produces output starting with "abc123"
    38→- Mixed case input "FooBar" produces output starting with "foobar"
    39→
    40→---
    41→
    42→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    43→**Priority**: Must Have
    44→**User Type**: Developer
    45→**Description**: The slugify function must replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    46→
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, improving readability while maintaining URL safety. Both spaces (from natural text) and underscores (from identifiers) should be normalized to the same separator.
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- Single space " " is replaced with single hyphen "-"
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces "  " are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    52→- Underscores "_" are replaced with hyphens "-"
    53→- Double underscores "__" are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    54→- Mixed whitespace and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    55→
    56→---
    57→
    58→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal
    59→**Priority**: Must Have
    60→**User Type**: Developer
    61→**Description**: The slugify function must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen.
    62→
    63→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause issues in URLs, filesystems, and databases. Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility.
    64→
    65→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    66→- Exclamation marks "!" are removed from output
    67→- Commas "," are removed from output
    68→- Periods "." are removed from output
    69→- Apostrophes "'" are removed from output
    70→- Any punctuation or special characters not in [a-z0-9-] are removed
    71→- Unicode/accented characters are removed (not transliterated)
    72→
    73→---
    74→
    75→### REQ-004: Hyphen Deduplication
    76→**Priority**: Must Have
    77→**User Type**: Developer
    78→**Description**: The slugify function must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    79→
    80→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens can result from removing special characters between words or from consecutive whitespace. Collapsing them improves readability and consistency.
    81→
    82→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    83→- Input "a---b" produces output "a-b"
    84→- Input "a--b" produces output "a-b"
    85→- Any sequence of two or more hyphens is replaced with exactly one hyphen
    86→- This deduplication applies after all other character transformations
    87→
    88→---
    89→
    90→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
    91→**Priority**: Must Have
    92→**User Type**: Developer
    93→**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the final output.
    94→
    95→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at string boundaries. They serve no semantic purpose and should be removed for cleaner output.
    96→
    97→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    98→- Input "-hello" produces output "hello"
    99→- Input "hello-" produces output "hello"
   100→- Input "-hello-" produces output "hello"
   101→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
   102→- Interior hyphens are preserved

   108→### STORY-001: Convert User Input to URL Slug
   109→**As a** web application developer

# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

## Overview

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Feature Name**: String Slugification Utility
**Priority**: Must Have
**Target Users**: Developers using the utility module

### Summary

Add a pure utility function that converts arbitrary text strings into URL-safe slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.

### Business Context

URL-safe slugs are essential for creating readable, consistent identifiers in URLs, filenames, database keys, and routing systems. This utility will provide a standardized transformation that developers can rely on across the codebase.

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must convert all uppercase letters to lowercase.

**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase for consistency and to avoid case-sensitivity issues across different systems and browsers.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input "Hello World" produces output starting with "hello world" (before other transformations)
- Input "ABC123" produces output starting with "abc123"
- Mixed case input "FooBar" produces output starting with "foobar"

---

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens.

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, improving readability while maintaining URL safety. Both spaces (from natural text) and underscores (from identifiers) should be normalized to the same separator.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Single space " " is replaced with single hyphen "-"
- Multiple consecutive spaces "  " are replaced with single hyphen "-"
- Underscores "_" are replaced with hyphens "-"
- Double underscores "__" are replaced with single hyphen "-"
- Mixed whitespace and underscores are normalized to single hyphens

---

### REQ-003: Special Character Removal
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen.

**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause issues in URLs, filesystems, and databases. Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Exclamation marks "!" are removed from output
- Commas "," are removed from output
- Periods "." are removed from output
- Apostrophes "'" are removed from output
- Any punctuation or special characters not in [a-z0-9-] are removed
- Unicode/accented characters are removed (not transliterated)

---

### REQ-004: Hyphen Deduplication
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.

**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens can result from removing special characters between words or from consecutive whitespace. Collapsing them improves readability and consistency.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input "a---b" produces output "a-b"
- Input "a--b" produces output "a-b"
- Any sequence of two or more hyphens is replaced with exactly one hyphen
- This deduplication applies after all other character transformations

---

### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer
**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the final output.

**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at string boundaries. They serve no semantic purpose and should be removed for cleaner output.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input "-hello" produces output "hello"
- Input "hello-" produces output "hello"
- Input "-hello-" produces output "hello"
- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
- Interior hyphens are preserved

---

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Convert User Input to URL Slug
**As a** web application developer
**I want** to convert user-provided titles into URL-safe slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN a blog post title "Hello, World!"
- WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
- THEN I receive "hello-world"

---

### STORY-002: Normalize Identifier Strings
**As a** system integrator
**I want** to normalize mixed-format identifiers
**So that** I have consistent keys for database records or file names

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN an identifier "Foo__Bar  "
- WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar  ")
- THEN I receive "foo-bar"

---

### STORY-003: Clean Complex Input
**As a** data processing developer
**I want** to handle messy input with repeated delimiters
**So that** the output is always clean and predictable

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN input with multiple consecutive hyphens "a---b"
- WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
- THEN I receive "a-b"

---

## Constraints

### Technical Constraints
- Function must be pure (no side effects)
- Function must be synchronous (no async operations)
- Function must handle empty strings gracefully
- Function must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module

### Business Constraints
- Must follow existing project patterns (camelCase naming, TypeScript strict mode)
- Must include comprehensive test coverage in `src/utils.test.ts`
- No external dependencies (use built-in string methods only)

---

## Success Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| Test Coverage | 100% | All transformation rules covered by unit tests |
| Code Quality | Pass TypeScript strict mode | No type errors or warnings |
| API Clarity | Single function signature | `slugify(text: string): string` |

---

## Examples

| Input | Expected Output |
|-------|-----------------|
| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` |
| `"Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` |
| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` |
| `"  spaces  "` | `"spaces"` |
| `"ABC123"` | `"abc123"` |
| `"test_case"` | `"test-case"` |
| `"---"` | `""` (empty string) |
| `""` | `""` (empty string) |

---

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:

- Unicode normalization or transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
- Custom separator characters (only hyphen is supported)
- Maximum length enforcement or truncation
- Uniqueness guarantees or collision detection
- Locale-specific transformations
- Configuration options or customization

---

## AFK Mode Decisions

This requirements document was generated in AFK (away-from-keyboard) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:

### Decision 1: PRD Association
**Point**: No PRD directory found
**Choice**: Continue without PRD association
**Rationale**: The `.rp1/work/prds/` directory does not exist, indicating this is a standalone feature request not tied to a specific product requirements document.

### Decision 2: Empty String Handling
**Point**: Behavior for empty string input not specified
**Choice**: Return empty string for empty input
**Rationale**: An empty string contains no characters to transform, so returning an empty string is the most logical and consistent behavior.

### Decision 3: All-Special-Character Input
**Point**: Behavior when input contains only special characters not specified
**Choice**: Return empty string after all characters are removed
**Rationale**: Following the transformation rules (remove non-alphanumeric/hyphen characters, trim hyphens) naturally leads to an empty string, which is consistent and predictable.

### Decision 4: Function Signature
**Point**: Return type and parameter types not explicitly specified
**Choice**: `slugify(text: string): string`
**Rationale**: TypeScript convention and project patterns indicate strict typing. String input and string output are the most natural types for text transformation utilities.

### Decision 5: Target Module
**Point**: Implementation location not specified beyond "utility"
**Choice**: Add to existing `src/utils.ts` module
**Rationale**: Knowledge base indicates `src/utils.ts` is the designated location for "pure functions providing reusable logic," which matches the nature of this slugify function.

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-27

## Summary

Implement a pure `slugify` function in the existing utils module that transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs through a sequential chain of string transformations: lowercase conversion, whitespace/underscore normalization to hyphens, special character removal, hyphen deduplication, and boundary trimming. The approach uses native JavaScript string methods and regex patterns with no external dependencies, maintaining consistency with the existing codebase patterns.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Input["Input String"] --> LC["toLowerCase()"]
    LC --> WS["Replace spaces/underscores"]
    WS --> SC["Remove special chars"]
    SC --> DD["Deduplicate hyphens"]
    DD --> TR["Trim boundary hyphens"]
    TR --> Output["Output Slug"]
```

|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | utils.ts | Any module | `slugify(text: string): string` - returns URL-safe slug |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-27

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Transformation order | lowercase -> replace whitespace/underscores -> remove special chars -> dedupe hyphens -> trim | This order ensures each step processes the output of the previous step correctly. Lowercasing first simplifies the special char regex. Deduplication must happen after all replacements that could create hyphens. Trimming must be last. | Different orderings tested; this order minimizes redundant operations |
| D2 | Regex vs iterative | Single-pass regex replacements | Native regex in JavaScript is optimized and concise. Chain of replace() calls is idiomatic and readable. | Character-by-character iteration would be verbose and slower |
| D3 | Whitespace pattern | `/[\s_]+/g` | Matches all whitespace characters (space, tab, newline) plus underscores in one pattern. The `+` quantifier handles multiple consecutive occurrences. | Separate patterns for space and underscore would require two replace calls |
| D4 | Special char pattern | `/[^a-z0-9-]/g` | Negated character class removes everything except lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Applied after lowercase conversion so no need for A-Z. | Allowlist approach would be more verbose |
| D5 | Hyphen deduplication | `/-+/g` replaced with `-` | Matches one or more hyphens and replaces with single hyphen. Handles both deduplication and edge cases from special char removal. | Lookahead assertions would be more complex |
| D6 | Boundary trim approach | `replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')` | Single regex handles both leading and trailing hyphens. More concise than separate replace calls or trim-like functions. | Two separate replace calls; substring manipulation |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Implementation location | src/utils.ts | KB modules.md | KB specifies utils.ts as the designated location for pure reusable functions |
| Function naming | camelCase (slugify) | KB patterns.md | Project convention for function names is camelCase |
| Test location | src/utils.test.ts | KB patterns.md | Tests co-located with source as *.test.ts per project convention |
| Test framework | Bun built-in (describe/test/expect) | KB patterns.md | Project uses Bun's native test runner, no external test libraries |
| TypeScript strictness | strict mode | KB patterns.md | Project enforces TypeScript strict mode |
| Dependencies | None (built-in string methods only) | Requirements constraint | Requirements explicitly prohibit external dependencies |

    18→### Summary
    19→
    20→Add a pure utility function that converts arbitrary text strings into URL-safe slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    21→
    22→### Business Context
    23→
    24→URL-safe slugs are essential for creating readable, consistent identifiers in URLs, filenames, database keys, and routing systems. This utility will provide a standardized transformation that developers can rely on across the codebase.
    25→
    26→## Requirements
    27→
    28→### REQ-001: Text Normalization
    29→**Priority**: Must Have
    30→**User Type**: Developer
    31→**Description**: The slugify function must convert all uppercase letters to lowercase.
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase for consistency and to avoid case-sensitivity issues across different systems and browsers.
    34→
    35→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    36→- Input "Hello World" produces output starting with "hello world" (before other transformations)
    37→- Input "ABC123" produces output starting with "abc123"
    38→- Mixed case input "FooBar" produces output starting with "foobar"
    39→
    40→---
    41→
    42→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    43→**Priority**: Must Have
    44→**User Type**: Developer
    45→**Description**: The slugify function must replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    46→
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, improving readability while maintaining URL safety. Both spaces (from natural text) and underscores (from identifiers) should be normalized to the same separator.
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- Single space " " is replaced with single hyphen "-"
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces "  " are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    52→- Underscores "_" are replaced with hyphens "-"
    53→- Double underscores "__" are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    54→- Mixed whitespace and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    55→
    56→---
    57→
    58→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal
    59→**Priority**: Must Have
    60→**User Type**: Developer
    61→**Description**: The slugify function must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen.
    62→
    63→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause issues in URLs, filesystems, and databases. Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility.
    64→
    65→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    66→- Exclamation marks "!" are removed from output
    67→- Commas "," are removed from output
    68→- Periods "." are removed from output
    69→- Apostrophes "'" are removed from output
    70→- Any punctuation or special characters not in [a-z0-9-] are removed
    71→- Unicode/accented characters are removed (not transliterated)
    72→

    74→

    76→**Priority**: Must Have
    77→**User Type**: Developer
    78→**Description**: The slugify function must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    79→
    80→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens can result from removing special characters between words or from consecutive whitespace. Collapsing them improves readability and consistency.

   118→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}, TASK_IDS={TASK_UNIT_IDS}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, REWRITE_COMMITS={GIT_COMMIT}, PREVIOUS_FEEDBACK={PREVIOUS_FEEDBACK}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   119→
   120→Re-run task-reviewer for the same unit. On second failure, escalate per §4.3.7.
   121→
   122→#### Reviewer Failure -- Pipelined Path
   123→
   124→When reviewer(k) returns `FAILURE` or malformed while builder(k+1) is in flight:
   125→
   126→1. **Wait** for builder(k+1) to complete. Do not dispatch anything new.
   127→2. **Mark dependencies stale**: any unit whose `depends_on` includes task IDs from unit k is not-ready until k passes review. The already-built k+1's review is deferred until k is resolved.
   128→3. **Run the retry path for unit k** using the same attempt/max logic as the sequential path above.
   129→4. If k passes retry: add k's task IDs to `COMPLETED_UNIT_TASK_IDS`, recalculate the ready set, then dispatch reviewer for the already-built k+1 unit.
   130→5. If k's retry is exhausted: escalate per §4.3.7. The already-built k+1 unit is abandoned along with k.
   131→
   132→#### Exhausted-Retry Escalation {#s4-3-7}
   133→
   134→Escalate without marking parent `implementation` failed while recovery remains.
   135→
   136→- Interactive: emit `waiting_for_user` on `implementation` with prompt "Task review failed after retry. Repair, Skip task, or Stop?" and context about the failing task unit. Then emit `implementation` waiting with `task_unit: "{TASK_UNIT_IDS}"` and `reason: "review_retry_exhausted"`. STOP with `/build {FEATURE_ID}` resume instructions.
   137→- AFK: if an explicit skip policy exists, record the skipped `TASK_UNIT_IDS` as release follow-ups; otherwise emit parent `implementation` failed only because no skip/repair path remains.
   138→
   139→#### Pipelining Rules
   140→
   141→1. **Never two builders concurrently** (serial mode). At most one task-builder may be in flight at any time in the default serial-pipelined path. The only concurrency is one reviewer alongside one builder on different units.
   142→2. **Never reviewer and builder on the same unit.** A unit's reviewer dispatches only after that unit's builder completes.
   143→3. **Dependency gate.** A unit whose `depends_on` contains task IDs from unit k must not begin building until k's reviewer returns `SUCCESS`.
   144→4. **Failure isolation.** When a pipelined reviewer(k) fails, wait for the in-flight builder(k+1) to finish, then resolve k's retry before any new dispatch.
   145→5. **Max two builders** (parallel-wave mode only). Parallel-wave mode dispatches at most two builders concurrently -- one on the primary `codeRoot`, one on a worktree `codeRoot`. Never three or more.
   146→6. **Parallel mode requires GIT_COMMIT=true and clean tree.** Without atomic commits the integration rebase has nothing to replay. A dirty working tree prevents worktree creation.
   147→7. **Overlapping file lists never concurrent.** If two units' task file lists share any source file path, they MUST NOT be in flight together — this applies to pipelined reviewer(k) ∥ builder(k+1) dispatch as well as parallel-wave builders. Fall back to strictly serial dispatch for those units.
   148→8. **Serial fallback.** When in doubt about preconditions, file overlap, or worktree health, fall back to the serial pipelined path. Parallel-wave is an optimization, not a requirement.
   149→9. **Emit namespacing unchanged.** Both primary and secondary builders emit with the same `task-builder:` step prefix. The `--unit` parameter distinguishes their events.
   150→10. **Default no-commit builds are serial.** When `GIT_COMMIT=false`, parallel groups in `tasks.md` describe dependency windows, but builder execution stays serial-pipelined because there is no atomic commit to replay from a worktree.
   151→
   152→#### Parallel-Wave Mode
   153→
   154→When ALL of the following preconditions are met, dispatch two builders concurrently instead of one:
   155→
   156→1. `GIT_COMMIT` is `true`.
   157→2. The working tree at `codeRoot` is clean (no unstaged or uncommitted changes).
   158→3. The ready set contains 2+ units with no mutual dependency (neither unit's `depends_on` includes the other's task IDs).
   159→4. The two candidate units' task file lists have no overlapping source file paths.
   160→
   161→**Trigger**: At the start of each dispatch cycle, before selecting a serial unit, compute the current ready wave. If at least two ready units are mutually independent and file-disjoint, dispatch the first unit as primary builder(k) on `codeRoot` and the second unit as secondary builder(k+1) on a worktree `codeRoot` in a single message.
   162→
   163→If fewer than two ready units qualify, use the standard serial-pipelined dispatch.
   164→
   165→**Dispatch**:
   166→
   167→Task tool:
   168→subagent_type: rp1-dev:task-builder
   169→prompt:
   170→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}, TASK_IDS={TASK_UNIT_IDS_K}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   171→
   172→Task tool:
   173→subagent_type: rp1-dev:task-builder
   174→prompt:
   175→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={worktreePath}, TASK_IDS={TASK_UNIT_IDS_K1}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   176→
   177→Wait for both builders to complete. Dispatch reviewer(k) on the primary `codeRoot` before integrating the secondary worktree. If reviewer(k) fails or is malformed, abandon the secondary worktree, retry or escalate k per the Reviewer Failure sections, and rebuild k+1 later from the serial path after k passes. If reviewer(k) succeeds, add k's task IDs to `COMPLETED_UNIT_TASK_IDS`, then integrate the secondary worktree per `references/parallel-builders.md` and dispatch reviewer(k+1) on the primary `codeRoot`.
   178→
   179→**Integration order**: After both builders finish and reviewer(k) succeeds, integrate the worktree branch (k+1) onto the primary branch per the Integration section in `references/parallel-builders.md`. If integration fails, apply the Conflict Fallback procedure (discard worktree, rebuild k+1 serially). Then dispatch reviewer(k+1) using the standard serial or pipelined path.
   180→
   181→See `references/parallel-builders.md` for the full worktree lifecycle protocol: creation, CODE_ROOT routing, integration, conflict fallback, cleanup, and failure handling.
   182→
   183→### §4.4 Post-Build
   184→
   185→Documentation tasks from `TASK_PLAN.documentation_tasks`:
   186→
   187→- Complete only through a declared supported workflow.
   188→- Current build has no declared docs implementation workflow; create `documentation_followups` from each docs task with `id`, `title`, `target`, `acceptance_refs`, `dependencies`, and `blocks_release = false`.
   189→- Carry `documentation_followups` into readiness/release `manual_items`.
   190→- Do not spawn undeclared documentation agents.
   191→
   192→### §4.5 Cleanup Manifest Generation
   193→
   194→After builders, reviewers, and documentation follow-up collection finish, generate the durable cleanup handoff before verification:
   195→
   196→```bash

   198→  --code-root "{codeRoot}" \
   199→  --out "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-001.json" \
   200→  --status-out "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-status.json" \

   202→  --baseline "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-baseline.json"
   203→```
   204→

If `data.status == "created"` with `files > 0` and `ownedLineCount > 0`, `comment-cleaner` may participate using `data.manifestPath`. If `data.status == "skipped"`, preserve `statusPath`/`skipReason` for the aggregator. On failure: set skipped with `skipReason: "change_manifest_generate_failed"`, `files: 0`, `ownedLineCount: 0`.
   206→
   207→### §4.6 Verification And Readiness
   208→
   209→#### Step 1 — Resolve comment-cleaner participation
   210→
   211→Evaluate the cleanup manifest result BEFORE dispatching any verification agent. Comment-cleaner participates only when ALL of: `cleanup_manifest_result.data.status == "created"`, `cleanup_manifest_result.data.files > 0`, `cleanup_manifest_result.data.ownedLineCount > 0`, and `cleanup_manifest_result.data.manifestPath` is present. Do not dispatch comment-cleaner with branch, unstaged, commit-range, base-branch, mode, or commit parameters; the generated manifest is the only safe cleanup boundary.

   288→## §PHASE-4: Release

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    14→**Feature Name**: String Slugification Utility
    15→**Priority**: Must Have
    16→**Target Users**: Developers using the utility module
    17→
    18→### Summary
    19→
    20→Add a pure utility function that converts arbitrary text strings into URL-safe slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    21→
    22→### Business Context
    23→
    24→URL-safe slugs are essential for creating readable, consistent identifiers in URLs, filenames, database keys, and routing systems. This utility will provide a standardized transformation that developers can rely on across the codebase.
    25→
    26→## Requirements
    27→
    28→### REQ-001: Text Normalization
    29→**Priority**: Must Have
    30→**User Type**: Developer
    31→**Description**: The slugify function must convert all uppercase letters to lowercase.
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase for consistency and to avoid case-sensitivity issues across different systems and browsers.
    34→
    35→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    36→- Input "Hello World" produces output starting with "hello world" (before other transformations)
    37→- Input "ABC123" produces output starting with "abc123"
    38→- Mixed case input "FooBar" produces output starting with "foobar"
    39→
    40→---
    41→
    42→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    43→**Priority**: Must Have
    44→**User Type**: Developer
    45→**Description**: The slugify function must replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    46→
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, improving readability while maintaining URL safety. Both spaces (from natural text) and underscores (from identifiers) should be normalized to the same separator.
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- Single space " " is replaced with single hyphen "-"
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces "  " are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    52→- Underscores "_" are replaced with hyphens "-"
    53→- Double underscores "__" are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    54→- Mixed whitespace and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    55→
    56→---
    57→
    58→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal
    59→**Priority**: Must Have
    60→**User Type**: Developer
    61→**Description**: The slugify function must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen.
    62→
    63→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause issues in URLs, filesystems, and databases. Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility.
    64→
    65→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    66→- Exclamation marks "!" are removed from output
    67→- Commas "," are removed from output
    68→- Periods "." are removed from output
    69→- Apostrophes "'" are removed from output
    70→- Any punctuation or special characters not in [a-z0-9-] are removed
    71→- Unicode/accented characters are removed (not transliterated)
    72→
    73→---
    74→
    75→### REQ-004: Hyphen Deduplication
    76→**Priority**: Must Have
    77→**User Type**: Developer
    78→**Description**: The slugify function must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    79→
    80→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens can result from removing special characters between words or from consecutive whitespace. Collapsing them improves readability and consistency.
    81→
    82→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    83→- Input "a---b" produces output "a-b"
    84→- Input "a--b" produces output "a-b"
    85→- Any sequence of two or more hyphens is replaced with exactly one hyphen
    86→- This deduplication applies after all other character transformations
    87→
    88→---
    89→
    90→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
    91→**Priority**: Must Have
    92→**User Type**: Developer
    93→**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the final output.
    94→
    95→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at string boundaries. They serve no semantic purpose and should be removed for cleaner output.
    96→
    97→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    98→- Input "-hello" produces output "hello"
    99→- Input "hello-" produces output "hello"
   100→- Input "-hello-" produces output "hello"
   101→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
   102→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   103→
   104→---
   105→
   106→## User Stories
   107→
   108→### STORY-001: Convert User Input to URL Slug
   109→**As a** web application developer
   110→**I want** to convert user-provided titles into URL-safe slugs
   111→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   112→
   113→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   114→- GIVEN a blog post title "Hello, World!"
   115→- WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
   116→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   117→
   118→---
   119→
   120→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifier Strings
   121→**As a** system integrator
   122→**I want** to normalize mixed-format identifiers
   123→**So that** I have consistent keys for database records or file names
   124→
   125→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   126→- GIVEN an identifier "Foo__Bar  "
   127→- WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar  ")
   128→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   129→
   130→---
   131→
   132→### STORY-003: Clean Complex Input
   133→**As a** data processing developer
   134→**I want** to handle messy input with repeated delimiters
   135→**So that** the output is always clean and predictable
   136→
   137→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   138→- GIVEN input with multiple consecutive hyphens "a---b"
   139→- WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   140→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   141→
   142→---
   143→
   144→## Constraints
   145→
   146→### Technical Constraints
   147→- Function must be pure (no side effects)
   148→- Function must be synchronous (no async operations)
   149→- Function must handle empty strings gracefully
   150→- Function must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   151→
   152→### Business Constraints
   153→- Must follow existing project patterns (camelCase naming, TypeScript strict mode)
   154→- Must include comprehensive test coverage in `src/utils.test.ts`
   155→- No external dependencies (use built-in string methods only)
   156→
   157→---
   158→
   159→## Success Metrics
   160→
   161→| Metric | Target | Measurement |
   162→|--------|--------|-------------|
   163→| Test Coverage | 100% | All transformation rules covered by unit tests |
   164→| Code Quality | Pass TypeScript strict mode | No type errors or warnings |
   165→| API Clarity | Single function signature | `slugify(text: string): string` |
   166→
   167→---
   168→
   169→## Examples
   170→
   171→| Input | Expected Output |
   172→|-------|-----------------|
   173→| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` |
   174→| `"Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` |
   175→| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` |
   176→| `"  spaces  "` | `"spaces"` |
   177→| `"ABC123"` | `"abc123"` |
   178→| `"test_case"` | `"test-case"` |
   179→| `"---"` | `""` (empty string) |
   180→| `""` | `""` (empty string) |
   181→
   182→---
   183→
   184→## Out of Scope
   185→
   186→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   187→
   188→- Unicode normalization or transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
   189→- Custom separator characters (only hyphen is supported)
   190→- Maximum length enforcement or truncation
   191→- Uniqueness guarantees or collision detection

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Convert a string to a URL-safe slug.
 *
 * Transforms arbitrary text into URL-safe slugs by:
 * - Converting to lowercase
 * - Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * - Removing non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens)
 * - Collapsing consecutive hyphens
 * - Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The input string to slugify
 * @returns A URL-safe slug string
 *
 * @example
 * slugify("Hello, World!") // returns "hello-world"
 * slugify("Foo__Bar  ") // returns "foo-bar"
 * slugify("a---b") // returns "a-b"
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, "")
    .replace(/-+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
}

- [x] **T1**: Implement slugify function with test-first coverage `[complexity:medium]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#component-plan](design.md#component-plan), [design.md#validation-plan](design.md#validation-plan)

    **Acceptance Refs**: REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005

    **Depends On**: -

    **Effort**: 6 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] Function exported from `src/utils.ts` with signature `slugify(text: string): string`
    - [ ] Test suite in `src/utils.test.ts` covers all 10 validation scenarios from design.md
    - [ ] REQ-001: Lowercase conversion works correctly (e.g., "Hello" -> "hello")
    - [ ] REQ-002: Spaces and underscores replaced with single hyphens
    - [ ] REQ-002: Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores collapsed to single hyphen
    - [ ] REQ-003: Special characters removed (only [a-z0-9-] remain)
    - [ ] REQ-004: Multiple consecutive hyphens deduplicated to single hyphen
    - [ ] REQ-005: Leading and trailing hyphens removed from output
    - [ ] Empty string input returns empty string
    - [ ] All-special-character input returns empty string (e.g., "---" -> "")
    - [ ] Tests pass: `bun test src/utils.test.ts`
    - [ ] TypeScript strict mode passes with no errors

    **Implementation Summary**

    **Files Modified**:
    - `src/utils.ts`: Added pure `slugify(text: string): string` function with JSDoc documentation
    - `src/utils.test.ts`: Added 16 comprehensive unit tests covering all requirements

    **Approach**:
    Implemented using TDD methodology with a sequential chain of five regex transformations:
    1. `.toLowerCase()` - converts all characters to lowercase (REQ-001)
    2. `.replace(/[\s_]+/g, "-")` - normalizes spaces and underscores to single hyphens (REQ-002)
    3. `.replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, "")` - removes all non-alphanumeric characters except hyphens (REQ-003)
    4. `.replace(/-+/g, "-")` - collapses consecutive hyphens into single hyphens (REQ-004)
    5. `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "")` - trims leading and trailing hyphens (REQ-005)

    **Test Coverage**:
    - REQ-001: 3 tests for lowercase conversion
    - REQ-002: 4 tests for space/underscore replacement and collapse
    - REQ-003: 4 tests for special character removal
    - REQ-004: 2 tests for hyphen deduplication
    - REQ-005: 3 tests for leading/trailing hyphen trimming
    - Edge cases: empty string, all-special-chars, complex mixed input, interior hyphen preservation

    **Validation**: All 16 tests pass (`bun test`). TypeScript strict mode enabled. No external dependencies.

    **Status**: ✅ Complete

    **Execution Flow**

    ```mermaid
    stateDiagram-v2
        [*] --> T1
        T1: T1 - Implement slugify function with test-first coverage
        T1 --> [*]
    ```

     8→
     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    14→**Feature Name**: String Slugification Utility
    15→**Priority**: Must Have
    16→**Target Users**: Developers using the utility module
    17→
    18→### Summary
    19→
    20→Add a pure utility function that converts arbitrary text strings into URL-safe slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    21→
    22→### Business Context
    23→
    24→URL-safe slugs are essential for creating readable, consistent identifiers in URLs, filenames, database keys, and routing systems. This utility will provide a standardized transformation that developers can rely on across the codebase.
    25→
    26→## Requirements
    27→
    28→### REQ-001: Text Normalization
    29→**Priority**: Must Have
    30→**User Type**: Developer
    31→**Description**: The slugify function must convert all uppercase letters to lowercase.
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase for consistency and to avoid case-sensitivity issues across different systems and browsers.
    34→
    35→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    36→- Input "Hello World" produces output starting with "hello world" (before other transformations)
    37→- Input "ABC123" produces output starting with "abc123"
    38→- Mixed case input "FooBar" produces output starting with "foobar"
    39→
    40→---
    41→
    42→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement
    43→**Priority**: Must Have
    44→**User Type**: Developer
    45→**Description**: The slugify function must replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    46→
    47→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, improving readability while maintaining URL safety. Both spaces (from natural text) and underscores (from identifiers) should be normalized to the same separator.
    48→
    49→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    50→- Single space " " is replaced with single hyphen "-"
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces "  " are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    52→- Underscores "_" are replaced with hyphens "-"
    53→- Double underscores "__" are replaced with single hyphen "-"
    54→- Mixed whitespace and underscores are normalized to single hyphens
    55→
    56→---
    57→
    58→### REQ-003: Special Character Removal
    59→**Priority**: Must Have
    60→**User Type**: Developer
    61→**Description**: The slugify function must remove any character that is not a letter (a-z), number (0-9), or hyphen.
    62→
    63→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause issues in URLs, filesystems, and databases. Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility.
    64→
    65→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    66→- Exclamation marks "!" are removed from output
    67→- Commas "," are removed from output
    68→- Periods "." are removed from output
    69→- Apostrophes "'" are removed from output
    70→- Any punctuation or special characters not in [a-z0-9-] are removed
    71→- Unicode/accented characters are removed (not transliterated)
    72→
    73→---
    74→
    75→### REQ-004: Hyphen Deduplication
    76→**Priority**: Must Have
    77→**User Type**: Developer
    78→**Description**: The slugify function must collapse multiple consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    79→
    80→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens can result from removing special characters between words or from consecutive whitespace. Collapsing them improves readability and consistency.
    81→
    82→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    83→- Input "a---b" produces output "a-b"
    84→- Input "a--b" produces output "a-b"
    85→- Any sequence of two or more hyphens is replaced with exactly one hyphen
    86→- This deduplication applies after all other character transformations
    87→
    88→---
    89→
    90→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming
    91→**Priority**: Must Have
    92→**User Type**: Developer
    93→**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the final output.
    94→
    95→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens can result from removing special characters at string boundaries. They serve no semantic purpose and should be removed for cleaner output.
    96→
    97→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    98→- Input "-hello" produces output "hello"
    99→- Input "hello-" produces output "hello"
   100→- Input "-hello-" produces output "hello"
   101→- Multiple leading/trailing hyphens are all removed
   102→- Interior hyphens are preserved
   103→
   104→---
   105→
   106→## User Stories
   107→
   108→### STORY-001: Convert User Input to URL Slug
   109→**As a** web application developer
   110→**I want** to convert user-provided titles into URL-safe slugs
   111→**So that** I can create clean, readable URLs for content pages
   112→
   113→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   114→- GIVEN a blog post title "Hello, World!"
   115→- WHEN I call slugify("Hello, World!")
   116→- THEN I receive "hello-world"
   117→
   118→---
   119→
   120→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifier Strings
   121→**As a** system integrator
   122→**I want** to normalize mixed-format identifiers
   123→**So that** I have consistent keys for database records or file names
   124→
   125→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   126→- GIVEN an identifier "Foo__Bar  "
   127→- WHEN I call slugify("Foo__Bar  ")
   128→- THEN I receive "foo-bar"
   129→
   130→---
   131→
   132→### STORY-003: Clean Complex Input
   133→**As a** data processing developer
   134→**I want** to handle messy input with repeated delimiters
   135→**So that** the output is always clean and predictable
   136→
   137→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   138→- GIVEN input with multiple consecutive hyphens "a---b"
   139→- WHEN I call slugify("a---b")
   140→- THEN I receive "a-b"
   141→
   142→---
   143→
   144→## Constraints
   145→
   146→### Technical Constraints
   147→- Function must be pure (no side effects)
   148→- Function must be synchronous (no async operations)
   149→- Function must handle empty strings gracefully
   150→- Function must be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module
   151→
   152→### Business Constraints
   153→- Must follow existing project patterns (camelCase naming, TypeScript strict mode)
   154→- Must include comprehensive test coverage in `src/utils.test.ts`
   155→- No external dependencies (use built-in string methods only)
   156→
   157→---
   158→
   159→## Success Metrics
   160→
   161→| Metric | Target | Measurement |
   162→|--------|--------|-------------|
   163→| Test Coverage | 100% | All transformation rules covered by unit tests |
   164→| Code Quality | Pass TypeScript strict mode | No type errors or warnings |
   165→| API Clarity | Single function signature | `slugify(text: string): string` |
   166→
   167→---
   168→
   169→## Examples
   170→
   171→| Input | Expected Output |
   172→|-------|-----------------|
   173→| `"Hello, World!"` | `"hello-world"` |
   174→| `"Foo__Bar  "` | `"foo-bar"` |
   175→| `"a---b"` | `"a-b"` |
   176→| `"  spaces  "` | `"spaces"` |
   177→| `"ABC123"` | `"abc123"` |
   178→| `"test_case"` | `"test-case"` |
   179→| `"---"` | `""` (empty string) |
   180→| `""` | `""` (empty string) |
   181→
   182→---
   183→
   184→## Out of Scope
   185→
   186→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   187→
   188→- Unicode normalization or transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
   189→- Custom separator characters (only hyphen is supported)
   190→- Maximum length enforcement or truncation
   191→- Uniqueness guarantees or collision detection
   192→- Locale-specific transformations
   193→- Configuration options or customization
   194→
   195→---
   196→
   197→## AFK Mode Decisions
   198→
   199→This requirements document was generated in AFK (away-from-keyboard) mode. The following decisions were made automatically:
   200→
   201→### Decision 1: PRD Association
   202→**Point**: No PRD directory found
   203→**Choice**: Continue without PRD association
   204→**Rationale**: The `.rp1/work/prds/` directory does not exist, indicating this is a standalone feature request not tied to a specific product requirements document.
   205→
   206→### Decision 2: Empty String Handling
   207→**Point**: Behavior for empty string input not specified
   208→**Choice**: Return empty string for empty input
   209→**Rationale**: An empty string contains no characters to transform, so returning an empty string is the most logical and consistent behavior.
   210→
   211→### Decision 3: All-Special-Character Input
   212→**Point**: Behavior when input contains only special characters not specified
   213→**Choice**: Return empty string after all characters are removed
   214→**Rationale**: Following the transformation rules (remove non-alphanumeric/hyphen characters, trim hyphens) naturally leads to an empty string, which is consistent and predictable.
   215→
   216→### Decision 4: Function Signature
   217→**Point**: Return type and parameter types not explicitly specified
   218→**Choice**: `slugify(text: string): string`
   219→**Rationale**: TypeScript convention and project patterns indicate strict typing. String input and string output are the most natural types for text transformation utilities.
   220→
   221→### Decision 5: Target Module
   222→**Point**: Implementation location not specified beyond "utility"
   223→**Choice**: Add to existing `src/utils.ts` module
